html:
A gold rush in the colony of Victoria, in southeast Australia, that began in 1851 and ran into the late 1860s. It turned Melbourne into one of the richest cities in the world.

Gold was found near Ballarat and Bendigo only months after Victoria split from New South Wales. Diggers came from Britain, Ireland, Germany, America and China, many straight from the California gold rush. Victoria's population grew several times over within a decade, and for a while the colony produced about a third of the world's gold.

The miners resented the licence fee they had to pay to dig. In 1854 that anger broke out at the Eureka Stockade near Ballarat, a short armed revolt that is still remembered as a birth of Australian democracy.

Chinese miners met hostility, special taxes and riots. That feeling fed straight into the later White Australia policy. Gold money paid for grand buildings, railways and "Marvellous Melbourne", and the crowded new city gave birth to Australian rules football in 1859.
sum: A gold rush in the colony of Victoria, in southeast Australia, that began in 1851 and ran into the late 1860s. It turned Melbourne into one of the richest cities in the world.
